scheme_name: Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units
description:
The Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units was launched by the Government of India in 2010. 

This scheme aims to promote dairy farming in the country. 

It specifically focuses on enhancing milk production and improving the quality of milk. 

The initiative is part of the National Dairy Plan which was initiated in 2012. 

The National Dairy Plan aims to increase milk production in India by 6 percent annually. 

The scheme is designed to provide financial assistance to dairy farmers. 

It encourages the establishment of modern dairy units that utilize advanced technology. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to support small and marginal farmers. 

The scheme aims to improve the livelihoods of dairy farmers. 

It also seeks to enhance the availability of quality milk in the market. 

The scheme targets the establishment of dairy units with a capacity of 10 to 50 animals. 

The financial assistance provided under the scheme is up to 25 percent of the total project cost. 

For SC/ST farmers, the assistance can go up to 33.33 percent. 

The maximum limit of assistance for a mini dairy unit is set at INR 1 lakh. 

For hi-tech dairy units, the maximum limit of assistance can reach up to INR 5 lakh. 

The scheme also aims to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It encourages the use of modern dairy farming practices. 

The eligibility criteria for the scheme include being a resident of India. 

Applicants must be engaged in dairy farming. 

There is no specific age limit for applicants. 

However, preference is given to small and marginal farmers. 

The income criteria for eligibility are not strictly defined. 

But applicants must demonstrate a commitment to dairy farming. 

The application process involves several steps. 

Interested applicants must first contact the local dairy development department. 

They need to obtain an application form which is available at the department's office. 

The completed application form must be submitted along with required documents. 

Required documents typically include identity proof and land ownership documents. 

Applicants may also need to provide a project report detailing the proposed dairy unit. 

The project report should outline the expected costs and returns. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the authorities. 

The review process may take several weeks. 

Upon approval, the financial assistance will be disbursed. 

The disbursement is usually made in installments based on project milestones. 

The first installment is often released after the establishment of the dairy unit. 

Subsequent installments are released based on the progress of the project. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

This department operates under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The contact details for the department can be found on their official website. 

The scheme is expected to contribute significantly to the dairy sector. 

It aims to enhance the productivity of dairy farms across the country. 

The scheme also promotes the use of artificial insemination and veterinary services. 

It encourages farmers to adopt better feeding and management practices. 

The implementation of this scheme is monitored at various levels. 

State governments are responsible for the execution of the scheme at the ground level. 

They are tasked with ensuring that the benefits reach the intended beneficiaries. 

The scheme has been instrumental in increasing the number of dairy units in rural areas. 

It has also played a role in improving the overall quality of milk production. 

The government has reported an increase in the income of dairy farmers due to this scheme. 

The scheme has been well-received in states with a strong dairy farming culture. 

States like Gujarat and Maharashtra have seen significant benefits from the scheme. 

The scheme aligns with the government's broader goals of rural development. 

It aims to reduce poverty and enhance food security in rural areas. 

The scheme is part of a larger framework of initiatives aimed at boosting agriculture. 

It complements other schemes such as the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi. 

The government continuously evaluates the impact of the scheme. 

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the implementation process. 

The scheme has also led to the establishment of cooperative dairy societies. 

These societies help in the collective marketing of milk and dairy products. 

The scheme encourages the formation of self-help groups among dairy farmers. 

This promotes knowledge sharing and collective problem-solving. 

The government provides training programs for farmers under this scheme. 

These programs focus on modern dairy farming techniques and management practices. 

The scheme has a significant impact on the rural economy. 

It helps in creating a sustainable livelihood for many families. 

The government aims to expand the reach of the scheme in the coming years. 

It plans to include more beneficiaries and enhance financial support. 

The scheme is a vital part of India's efforts to become self-sufficient in milk production. 

The dairy sector is crucial for the nutritional security of the population. 

The scheme is expected to play a pivotal role in achieving this goal. 

Overall the Scheme for Establishment of Hi-Tech and Mini Dairy Units is a comprehensive initiative. 

It addresses multiple aspects of dairy farming and rural development. 

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the livelihoods of dairy farmers. 

It aims to create a vibrant and sustainable dairy sector in India.
